title: Double the product's load-sensitive time limits (Git verification 20 s → 40 s, 10 s Engram deadlines → 20 s) and keep every derived relation
outcome: Decision (Greg, 2026-09-28, in Termal::Opus2's session, verbatim on this item): "no, let's double the limits / why ? / if CPU is high it will affect also the product, we don't want that / it's not just test only issue". Under CPU contention, git verification calls and Engram control calls miss their fixed deadlines, in the tests and in the running host alike. The retained-prompt pauses of 2026-09-28 were the 10 s admission durability fence (w-e0f80b315a6d). So the load-sensitive limits are doubled in the product, as Greg's explicit exception to CLAUDE.md's rule against larger timeouts, and every limit derived from them keeps its relation. Original observation (2026-09-26): 13 of 66 turn_checks tests failed under load, with "Git verification operation ls-files … bounded read deadline exceeded" after about 17.4 s of the 20 s shared budget had gone to earlier git calls. The same tests passed on an idle machine. The earlier fix direction, "do not raise the product's budget", is superseded by Greg's decision.
acceptance: Every limit derived from those, or required to exceed them, keeps its relation, stated in code where it is computed: the lifecycle settle wait stays one second above the call cap, the source-root naming budget covers two Git captures, the review-freeze observer stays five seconds above the freeze budget, and each MCP bridge wait for the review-freeze check, source-root naming, acceptance evaluation and submission exceeds the backend budget it waits on; the tests and docs that state the values follow.

On Greg's word (2026-09-28, recorded on this item), the running product's load-sensitive time limits are doubled: the shared Git verification budget from 20 s to 40 s, and the 10 s Engram deadlines to 20 s — the admission dispatch budget with its durability fence, the default control-call timeout and its configured cap, the readiness and Save absence-inspection budget, and the acceptance-policy read and write.
